5G is a couple of things put together. It's a number of standardized frequencies by which devices can communicate, and software protocols that is basically the "language and rules of parliament" that devices coordinate with each other.

The difference between 4G and 5G is that 5G uses frequencies that were until recently not easy to effectively use for communication. They require a more sophisticated protocol. Why? Because a higher frequency has higher bandwith, so this is an advantage over lower 4G frequencies. However, they are more likely to be blocked by everyday objects, like walls. Which makes it impractical if you don't have direct line of sight to the tower.

So, to make 5G practical, the protocol needs to be more robust. If you have line of sight to the tower, you connect to the tower normally. If not, then maybe you can route through a nearby 5G device that does have direct line of sight to the tower. If not, switch to 4G.
